extracted.intended_audience: inventors, startup founders, and U.S. patent applicants (including practitioners advising them)
extracted.subtask_short: provisional vs utility patent filing strategy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on choosing, drafting, and timing provisional (provisional) vs nonprovisional (utility) U.S. patent applications, including required disclosures, conversion timing, costs, and strategic tradeoffs for commercialization and investor interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Patent Application Characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application is a quick and inexpensive way to establish a U.S. filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristics listed: Not examined by USPTO; Cannot mature into a granted patent; Lower fees and less rigorous formal requirements; Establishes priority date for later non-provisional; Becomes abandoned 12 months after filing; Does not require formal claims (though strongly recommended). Use a provisional to secure an early filing date but understand it alone does not create enforceable patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprovisional (Utility) Patent Application Characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal patent application examined by USPTO to determine patentability and that can mature into a granted patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristics listed: Examined by USPTO; Can mature into a granted patent; Required for actual patent rights; Higher fees and stricter formal requirements; Examined under all statutory requirements (101, 102, 103, 112). Prepare a complete, rigorously drafted utility application if you intend to obtain enforceable rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: When Provisional Applications Are Useful
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations in which filing a provisional application is strategically advantageous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a provisional when you need to secure a filing date quickly (before disclosure); have a limited budget early in company life; want to test market interest before larger investment; are still refining the invention; need 12 months to develop product/seek funding; want to label 'Patent Pending'; or are establishing priority for later international filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: When Utility Applications Are Best
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations where filing a nonprovisional (utility) application is the appropriate next step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File a utility application when the invention is market-ready; you want to move directly toward patent protection; you need to enforce rights soon; competitors are close to launching similar technology; or you have full disclosure ready to claim. Utility filings carry greater legal and commercial weight than provisionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-Year Conversion Window (12-Month Priority Rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must file a utility patent application within 12 months of the filing date of the provisional patent application to receive priority benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file within the 12-month window forfeits the provisional's priority date. Calendar and docket this deadline; plan drafting and funding timelines accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure Adequacy for Priority Benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: You will only get an early filing date for claims that are supported by the disclosure in the provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be as complete as possible in the provisional. Consider what will ultimately be claimed in the utility application when drafting the provisional—insufficient disclosure means 'no priority for important claims.' Ensure the provisional's disclosure enables the claimed invention (written description and enablement).

rubrics_metrics.name: No New Matter / Cannot Add New Matter to Provisional
rubrics_metrics.description: New matter cannot be added to a provisional application to create priority for claims that were not supported in the provisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need to add material not present in the provisional, you must file a new application; you cannot rely on the provisional to support claims that depend on later-added subject matter. Draft provisionals with anticipated claim scope in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Pitfalls (weak provisional dangers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common failure modes specific to provisional applications that undermine priority and value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitfalls listed: A 'throwaway provisional' gives priority for nothing; Insufficient disclosure = no priority for important claims; Cannot add new matter to provisional (must file new application). Avoid filing thin provisionals just to hit a date—quality of disclosure matters for later claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Tradeoffs Between Provisional and Utility Filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative costs and budgeting considerations for provisional vs utility patent prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table items include: Filing Fee (small entity) — Provisional ~$140 vs Utility ~$830; Search Fee — None for provisional, required for utility; Examination Fee — None for provisional, required for utility; Drafting Cost — Provisional $1,500-5,000 vs Utility $8,000-25,000; Total to Grant — N/A (provisional) vs $15,000-50,000+ (utility). Use these figures to plan budgets; remember provisional lowers upfront cost but does not avoid later utility expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investor Perception of Filing Types
rubrics_metrics.description: How different filing stages are perceived by investors and impact fundraising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional filings support early-stage discussions; Utility filings carry greater weight during later funding rounds; Issued patents provide the highest signal value for investors. Consider investor timelines when choosing filing strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common Mistakes to Avoid in Provisional/Utility Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise list of frequent errors applicants make when using provisional and utility filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common mistakes listed: 1) Filing a 'thin' provisional with no real disclosure; 2) Failing to convert within 12 months; 3) Adding new matter to provisional (cannot be done); 4) Public disclosure between provisional and non-provisional outside US (loss of foreign rights); 5) Treating provisional as cheap 'patent pending' with no follow-through. Use this list as a checklist to avoid strategic and procedural errors that can destroy rights.
